done.title: Gooi tracks itself (CLI)
done.detail: The operations `status`, `open` and `close --used "<what it was used for>"` are edges over `.gooi/slices.json`, with a generic CLI surface (`surfaces/cli`). The CLI keeps this page's Open slice and Done sections in sync.
done.done: the owner closes this slice with `bun gooi close --used "..."`.
done.used: to check the status of the project

done.title: Tasks as markdown files
done.detail: Each task is tasks/<name>.md with a status and created header and free notes below. List, add and finish tasks through the same generic CLI, and editing a file by hand stays valid.
done.done: the owner tracks gooi's real next tasks in tasks/ and has finished one with the CLI.

done.title: Compile the gooi command into a Commander CLI
done.detail: Edges describe their inputs with JSON Schema. One step turns the edges into a command tree with chosen names and groups; a lowering edge emits a Commander program that calls the edges directly. The generated CLI replaces `bun gooi`.
done.done: the generated CLI replaces bun gooi for daily use by the owner and agents, and @gooi/cli is not in it.

done.title: See tasks in a browser
done.detail: The tasks app renders its listing to HTML through an HTML syntax tree, printed and parsed back. A compiled server runs the task list then render path on each request; titles are text, never markup.
done.done: the owner keeps the task page open while working and it shows current tasks, including hand edits and agent changes.
done.used: monitor the task list as it updates live

done.title: Task page in shadcn
done.detail: A shadcn mapping lowers the task page's HTML syntax tree to TSX using shadcn components, printed and parsed back, and the server renders it to HTML with Tailwind. renderTasks does not change.
done.done: the owner keeps the shadcn task page open instead of the plain one, and renderTasks is unchanged.
done.used: using shadcn now to monitor the list

done.title: Tell an agent, get a task
done.detail: An agent edge takes an ACP prompt and returns the turn's ACP session updates. Its toolbox of task edges becomes tools built from their JSON Schemas, and every tool call runs through invoke. Backings are host wiring: gooi's loop over Claude, then over the local model in OMLx, with no change to edges, toolbox or instructions. gooi agent tell exposes it.
done.done: the owner turns a real rant into tasks with gooi agent tell on Claude and on the local model in OMLx, with the same app code.
done.used: used both backings to try enriching the rac ACP output

done.title: Agent conversations on a swappable log
done.detail: Gooi's agent appends each turn's ACP notifications, the owner's prompt included, to a log interface: append with an expected length, read, list. JSONL files and SQLite both pass one law suite, and host wiring picks between them. gooi agent sessions and gooi agent show --session follow ACP's session list and load.
done.done: the owner reads a past agent conversation with gooi agent show on both JSONL and SQLite, with no app change.
done.used: reviewed my ongoing conversation with claude

done.title: Claude and OMLx in one room
done.detail: A room is a log stream of Matrix events: messages (m.room.message), members (m.room.member) and mentions (m.mentions). The owner posts from the CLI. Each mentioned agent reads the room through its own ACP session and answers under its own Matrix user ID. gooi room show reads the room back.
done.done: the owner has one real conversation with Claude and OMLx in one room and reads it back with gooi room show.
done.used: reviewed my ongoing conversation with both agents

done.title: A second host: tasks and a room for nooq
done.detail: Apps don't know where they run; a host composes them, like a compose file. gooi's own wiring moves to hosts/gooi. A second host, hosts/nooq, composes the tasks and room apps for nooq: nooq's own task folder and room logs, Claude and OMLx with nooq's task tools, exposed as its own Commander CLI. The apps lose what only gooi needs, and the room checks that the log and agents it is given have the right contracts.
done.done: the owner uses the nooq CLI to track a real nooq task and talk it through with the agents, and the tasks and room apps hold no gooi-specific code.
done.used: asked the nooq room to turn the BlockNote gap audit into nooq tasks
